questions.stem: A 58 year old woman has a 2 year history of leaking urine. She leaks a little when she coughs or lifts shopping, and on most days she also gets a sudden strong need to pass urine and sometimes wets herself before reaching the toilet. She gets up twice at night. Urine dipstick is normal.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Leakage with coughing (stress) plus sudden urgency with leakage (urge) is mixed incontinence, a common picture.

steps.x: The lead-in is: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer it wants before reading the options.

clues: leaks a little when she coughs
sudden strong need to pass urine
steps.x: **Cough leak = stress**; **urgency then leak = urge**. Both together = **mixed**.

elim: She can reach the toilet; the problem is the bladder and pelvic floor, not mobility or cognition.
No poor stream, dribbling or distended bladder.
Explains the cough leakage but not the sudden urgency.
Gives constant leakage, not leakage linked to triggers.

steps.x: **B. Mixed urinary incontinence.** Many patients have a mixed picture; treat the predominant symptom first.

questions.stem: A 61 year old woman leaks small amounts of urine when she jumps on a trampoline with her grandchildren and when she sneezes. Her periods stopped 9 years ago. Her BMI is 33 kg/m². She has no urgency, no frequency and no nocturia. Abdominal examination is normal and urine dipstick is negative.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Small-volume leakage on exertion or sneezing without urgency is stress incontinence; menopause and obesity are risk factors.

steps.x: The lead-in is: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer it wants before reading the options.
Leak with **raised intra-abdominal pressure**, no urgency. Risk factors: **menopause, obesity**.

elim: She is mobile and cognitively intact.
No retention, poor stream or palpable bladder.
No urgency, frequency or nocturia.
Dipstick is negative and there is no dysuria.

steps.x: **C. Stress incontinence.** Exertion/cough/sneeze leakage with no urgency = stress incontinence.

questions.stem: A 72 year old man with type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has a 5 month history of constantly dribbling urine and feeling he never empties his bladder. His stream is weak. questions.e: Constant dribbling, incomplete emptying and a palpable bladder mean chronic retention with overflow; diabetic neuropathy can make the detrusor underactive.

steps.x: The lead-in is: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer it wants before reading the options.
Dribbling + **distended bladder** = **overflow**. Prostate is small, so think **neuropathy** (diabetes) as the cause.

elim: He has a real bladder problem: a distended bladder from retention.

Leakage is constant, not with coughing or exertion.
No sudden urgency; the bladder is distended, not overactive.

steps.x: **C. Overflow incontinence.** Overflow incontinence comes from chronic retention, from obstruction or an atonic detrusor.

questions.stem: A 27 year old woman who recently moved to the UK has leaked urine continuously, day and night, for 4 months. questions.e: Constant leakage after a prolonged, obstructed labour is a vesicovaginal fistula: pressure necrosis creates a bladder-vagina tract.

**Constant** leakage with no trigger + **prolonged/difficult labour** = **vesicovaginal fistula**.

No urgency.

steps.x: **E. Vesicovaginal fistula.** Constant leakage after obstructed labour = fistula, confirmed with urinary dye studies.

questions.stem: An 81 year old man has severe knee osteoarthritis and walks slowly with a frame. Since moving to a house with the only toilet upstairs he has wet himself most days on the way to it. Normal bladder function + **mobility barrier** = **functional** incontinence.

questions.stem: A 49 year old office manager has a 6 month history of sudden urgency, often leaking before she reaches the toilet. She passes urine 12 times a day and gets up twice at night. questions.stem: A 67 year old woman has had type 1 diabetes for 40 years, with gastroparesis and postural hypotension. small volumes 10 to 14 times a day

questions.stem: A 77 year old man has a 6 month history of poor stream, hesitancy and post-void dribbling, and now leaks small amounts of urine through the day. He gets up four times at night. He has a mildly enlarged smooth prostate. His creatinine is normal.
